title: fix(plugin-approvals): a locked record's lines read as locked, and deleting the locked record still lands
body:
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 审批中的单据：它的明细行在「是否锁定」查询里也答「已锁定」，和服务端拒绝修改明细的结果一致；审批中删除整张单据又能成功，明细一起删掉、审批请求自动取消。
- 属于审批锁定的加固，替使用审批的业务用户解决「单据锁了但明细状态不一致」和「带明细的单据审批中删不掉」两个问题。
- 出错的话：要么明细被误报为锁定，要么带明细的单据删不掉；可直接撤回本次合并，只回到合并前的状态。
- 无

## What changes

The rule: **a locked record's lines are locked with it, and deleting the locked record itself still lands.** No node switch is added and no default moves: lines lock whenever the record's approval node locks the record, as `main` already enforces.

- **The lock read answers for a line.** `ApprovalService.getRecordLock` (the record-lock read behind `GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock` and `client.approvals.getRecordLock`) now answers `{ locked: true }` for a `master_detail` child row while its master is held by a locking pending approval. It used the record-lock judgement only, so it answered `{ locked: false }` for exactly the rows the detail-row lock refuses with `409 RECORD_LOCKED`. The new `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` (in `lifecycle-hooks.ts`) asks the hook's own question: the row's master edges, read off its FK columns as SYSTEM, each judged by the one shared lookup (`lockingRequestsForRecords`). The caller-scoped readability anchor is unchanged, so a row the caller cannot read still answers `null`, like a missing id.
- **Deleting the locked record lands again, with its lines.** The delete-cancel linkage cancels a record's pending request when the record is deleted (its ruling vetoed "forbid delete while pending"). The detail-row lock refused the `master_detail` cascade legs of that delete, so a locked record with lines could not be deleted (`409 RECORD_LOCKED`). The detail-row lock's `beforeDelete` now lets a cascade leg through on one edge only. That leg carries the engine's declared marker `ctx.referentialCascadeDelete`, and the detail object's single cascade-capable relation must be the `master_detail` edge to the held master, which makes the record being deleted that master. The leg must also run inside an open unit of work: a `ctx.transaction` handle the engine does not report closed. A delete with no open transaction is refused whole with `409 RECORD_LOCKED`, and the record, its lines and its pending request stay. That covers a datasource that declares `supports.transactionsUnsupported`, a cascade across datasources, a record and its lines together on a non-default datasource, and a handle whose unit has already finished. Every other shape is refused too: a junction under two cascading masters, or a line that also has a `lookup` declaring `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`. So deleting a different record never removes a held record's line, with one exception. When the held record is itself the child of a record whose delete cascades to it (a `master_detail` child, or a `lookup` child with `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`), deleting that parent removes the held record with its lines and cancels its request.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` now states that lines are locked with the record (insert / update / delete / reparent, the carried exemptions, `lookup` children untouched). It also states what deleting the record while pending does and when that delete is refused, that server code owning the transaction must not catch the refusal and commit over it, and that the lock read answers for a line.

## Why

A page reads the lock to decide whether to offer an edit, so the read must answer the same way the server refuses. And a pending record must stay deletable, because the delete-cancel linkage is the only route left once the record is locked.

## Tests

Each new pin was run against the base first (red), then with the fix (green), and each guard was ablated (red) and restored (`git diff HEAD` empty, blob equal to HEAD).

- `record-lock-read.integration.test.ts`: new top-level `describe` ("a locked record's lines are locked with it — the record-lock read answers for a detail row too"), 4 cases on the real `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()` rig, with two line objects added to it. Base: 2 failed / 6 passed (`expected { locked: false } to deeply equal { locked: true }`). Fix: 8 / 8. Ablating the new `|| detailRowHeldByLockingApproval(...)`: 2 failed, restored.
- `detail-row-lock.integration.test.ts`, four new top-level `describe`s:
  - "… deleting the record itself still lands", 5 cases: the held record deletes with its lines; the caller's own line delete is refused; a different record's cascade is refused; two fail-closed shapes, a junction under two masters and `master_detail` plus a cascading lookup, are refused with nothing removed. Base: the delete case failed (refused `RECORD_LOCKED`). Ablating the cascade yield: 1 failed. Ablating the sole-edge narrowing: 1 failed.
  - "… without a transaction the held record's delete is refused", 3 cases on a sqlite driver that declares `supports.transactionsUnsupported`: a held record with a later `restrict` row, a held record with lines only, and a control in which an unheld record deletes. Base: 2 failed (`DELETE_RESTRICTED`; the delete landed).
  - "… a closed unit's handle is no transaction", 1 case: a cascade split across two datasources, with a delete carrying the handle of a finished transaction. Base: `DELETE_RESTRICTED`.
  - "… a held record that is itself a detail row goes with its master", 1 case.
  - Ablating the transaction check turned the two no-transaction pins red (2 failed). Ablating the open-unit test (a closed unit's handle counted as open) turned the closed-handle pin red (1 failed, `DELETE_RESTRICTED`). Every ablation was restored.
- The existing insert / update / delete pins of that file were ablated one hook registration at a time: `beforeInsert` 3 failed, `beforeUpdate` 4 failed, `beforeDelete` 2 failed, each restored.
- Whole package at `d2056107`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: 126 files / 1822 tests passed. `typecheck` (incl. `check:test-typecheck`) OK.

## Acceptance notes

- **Withheld yield.** A locked record whose line object has a second relation that also cascades on delete stays undeletable while pending. So does one whose delete runs outside an open transaction. The engine does not tell a hook which record started a cascade, and outside a transaction a later refusal could not put the lines back. In both cases this refuses rather than risk a held line. The docs page says so.
- **Owner of the transaction.** Inside a transaction, the refusal is what keeps the lines. Server code that owns the transaction must not catch the refused delete and commit anyway; the hook cannot prevent that, and the docs state the rule.
- **Unchanged.** No node-level switch for the line lock and no change to its default: lines lock whenever the node locks the record. Decided documents are not locked; edits after the decision are not in this PR.
- **Pending approvers and the lines (read, measured).** The pending-approver read grant names the master record only. On the real service it answers `["held_sheet_a"]` for the master object and `[]` for its line object. An approver reads lines through the line object's own access: a `controlled_by_parent` detail follows the master's readability (source reading, not run on a kernel), and a `private` detail owned by the submitter is not readable to them.
- No console code changes, so no browser check is owed.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/record-lock-read.integration.test.ts src/detail-row-lock.integration.test.ts` should report 2 files and 29 tests passed.

Files to read first, by risk: `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts` (the `cascadeSource` hunk in `bindDetailRowLockHook` and `soleCascadeEdgeOf`), then `inOpenUnit` and `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval` beside it, then `approval-service.ts` `getRecordLock`.
